subject: physics_2
question_text: What is a.m.u? What is its equivalent energy?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: 1 u = 1.660539 × 10⁻²⁷ kg; E = uc² = 1.660539 × 10⁻²⁷ × (2.998 × 10⁸)² = 1.4924 × 10⁻¹⁰ J = 931.5 MeV. The book prints "1u = 931.5 MeV", which equates a mass with an energy; this card writes it as the ENERGY EQUIVALENT of 1 u, which is what the mark scheme means. The book's spacing "a.m.u ?" is written here without the space before the question mark.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Atomic mass unit
steps.mark_note: One twelfth of the mass of a ¹²C atom
lines: Atomic mass unit (u): one twelfth of the mass
of one neutral ¹²C atom is called one atomic
steps.margin_note: First mark. The definition must name carbon-12 and the factor one twelfth.
steps.why: Nuclear masses are all close to a whole number of nucleons, so a unit built from one nucleus makes every mass a number near A — that is why the scale is tied to ¹²C and not to the kilogram.
common_mistakes: Saying "one twelfth of a carbon atom" without naming ¹²C. The isotope matters.
Writing 1.66 × 10⁻²⁴ kg. That is the value in grams, not kilograms.

recall.must_convey: That one atomic mass unit is one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, equal to 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
accept: one twelfth of the mass of carbon twelve
one point six six into ten power minus twenty seven kilogram
u is defined from carbon twelve
reject: nine hundred thirty one point five mega electron volt

steps.memory_tip: Twelve nucleons in ¹²C, so one nucleon-sized unit is one twelfth of it.

steps.label: Equivalent energy
lines: By the relation E = mc², a mass of 1 u is
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The number 931.5 MeV is the one the examiner looks for.
steps.why: Every mass defect in this chapter is measured in u, so 931.5 MeV per u is the single conversion that turns a mass defect straight into a binding energy.
common_mistakes: Writing 931.5 eV or 931.5 J. The unit is MeV.
Saying 1 u equals 931.5 MeV of mass. Mass and energy are equivalent, not identical.

recall.must_convey: That the energy equivalent of one atomic mass unit is 931.5 MeV, obtained from E = mc².
accept: nine hundred thirty one point five mega electron volt

steps.memory_tip: 931.5 MeV per u is the exchange rate between mass defect and binding energy.

insider_note: Two marks, two facts: the definition tied to carbon-12, and the number 931.5 MeV from E = mc².
